audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows contradicted the why-text sitting next to them, and the packet logged the defect outright.
audit.why: whys[0] says Riven takes Level 1 while the row said Graves; whys[1] through whys[5] all describe Graves owning the lane while rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 said Skill or Riven; whys[6] says execution decides at two items while the row said Riven. The mirror settled the chart as Riven / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Graves / Skill and the packet chart agrees.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 flipped as one atomic group across both layers; Level 1 to 7/10, the Graves rows to 3/10, the two-item row to 5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two-item spike built Immortal Shieldbow while the entry's itemisation section builds Eclipse into Sterak's Gage.
audit.why: The spike has to arrive on the build the page actually recommends, or the timing never happens.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] rewritten around Eclipse into Sterak's Gage.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate strings claim Smoke Screen BLINDS Riven's autos and stops Runic Blade from connecting. It does not blind at all.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen: it creates a cloud that reduces sight range, and enemies caught in the initial impact take magic damage and are briefly slowed. There is no blind and no miss chance — every auto inside it lands and every Runic Blade charge still spends. The actual problem is that Riven cannot SEE Graves, so she chases a target she has lost. Told her autos whiff, a player stops attacking inside the smoke and gives up free damage; told the truth, she keeps swinging at the last known position and only worries about tracking him.
audit.corrected: whys[2], spikes[1] and wants.foe[1] rewritten to nearsight-plus-slow. The 'blind' claim is also in the 'mid' paragraph, flagged in notes.
sources: enemyKit W text (no blind, reduces sight range, slows on impact)

audit.whatIsWrong: Graves' passive was never used: his shotgun fires four bullets that CANNOT PASS THROUGH UNITS, and he has to reload.
audit.why: This is the single most concrete defensive tool Riven has in the matchup — standing so the minion wave is between her and Graves strips most of the shot, and his reload animation is a bigger free window than his dash cooldown. Neither appeared anywhere on the page.
audit.corrected: wants.you[1] now teaches the minion body-block; whys[3] repoints the punish window from Quickdraw to the reload.
sources: enemyKit P text 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units'

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] called Quickdraw a 'short cooldown' with no number.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16 seconds at rank 1, not short — what makes it feel permanent is that landed basic attacks lower its cooldown. Naming the mechanic tells the player why waiting it out fails while he is farming.
audit.corrected: whys[3] and spikes[1] now state the 16-second base and the auto-attack refund.
sources: enemyKit E cd '16/15/14/13/12' and text 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers the cooldown'

edits.before: Smoke screen blinds your Q autos mid-chain and Quickdraw resets his positioning — your full three-hit combo rarely completes cleanly against a competent Graves.
edits.after: Smoke Screen does not blind — it cuts your sight and slows you, so you lose him, not your autos. Quickdraw then resets his spacing and your chain dies.

edits.before: Quickdraw's short cooldown means he almost always has it available to escape or reposition; you are fighting on his terms unless he wastes it on a minion wave.
edits.after: Quickdraw is 16s at rank 1 but every landed auto shaves it, so it is up whenever he is farming — his reload, not his dash, is your real punish window.

edits.before: Graves's Quickdraw lets him dodge your W stun, reposition behind his smoke, and burst you with point-blank shotgun autos before you complete the Q chain.
edits.after: Quickdraw dodges your Ki Burst and refunds its own 16s cooldown off every auto — he resets spacing behind smoke and shotguns you before the Q chain lands.

edits.before: The lane is genuinely Skill at two items — your Eclipse + Immortal Shieldbow sustain lets you match his burst if you bait Quickdraw before committing W.
edits.after: The lane is genuinely Skill at two items — Eclipse into Sterak's Gage lets you eat the volley and match his burst if you bait Quickdraw before committing W.

edits.before: Use Valor (E) reactively to absorb his point-blank shotgun burst, not to gap-close through smoke
edits.after: Keep a minion between you — his four bullets cannot pass through units, so the wave eats the shot

edits.before: Use smoke screen (W) to blind your Q autos and prevent Runic Blade charges from connecting
edits.after: Drop Smoke Screen to nearsight you — you cannot see him to chase, and it slows you on impact

notes: The 'Smoke Screen blinds you' error also lives in the 'mid' paragraph ('his smoke blind cancels your Q auto weaving mid-chain') and 'late' still names Immortal Shieldbow's lifeline passive after spikes[3] moved to Sterak's Gage. I left both long paragraphs alone: rewriting them inside the +/-10% band is doable but the surrounding full-layer strings in this brief carry mojibake em dashes and I did not want to risk a stale-before rejection on a paragraph this long. Both are worth a byte-exact follow-up. Not asserted: whether Quickdraw can be used during Riven's Ki Burst stun — 'Land Quickdraw through or around your W stun' in wants.foe[0] implies it beats the stun, which the kits do not establish, so I left that string untouched.
